Quotes / Jean-Jacques Rousseau / Q0252

English

Everything is good as it leaves the hands of the Author of things; everything degenerates in the hands of man.
Thinker Jean-Jacques Rousseau
School Enlightenment
Source Émile I
Theme Nature
Another quotation More from this thinker

Context and commentary are editorial aids for reading. They do not replace the primary text or scholarly commentary.

Source context

This English passage is associated with Émile I, within the tradition of Enlightenment. The wording below is a verified rendering prepared for careful reading rather than a claim of unique translation authority.

A short reading

Read in the register of nature, the sentence asks the reader to test an assumption rather than to collect a slogan. In Jean-Jacques Rousseau's wider work, similar claims are usually offered as prompts for judgment: what would have to be true for the sentence to hold, and what would follow if it did?
